{"explanation": "Restoring the dot check in hasCustomProtocol ensures that URLs with a dot in the scheme (like 'foo.bar:baz') are not treated as custom protocols, allowing them to be processed through normalization (which throws an error for invalid URLs) or normalized correctly (like 'foo.bar://' becoming 'http://foo.bar'). This fixes both reported regressions.", "edits": [{"path": "index.js", "old": "	return protocol.endsWith(':')
		&& !supportedProtocols.has(protocol);", "new": "	return protocol.endsWith(':')
		&& !protocol.includes('.')
		&& !supportedProtocols.has(protocol);"}]}
